The True Cost of In-Port Emissions

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (269 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How current shore power rules cost hundreds of millions every year in health and climate damages.
  • Air pollution and climate emissions from ships at berth impose a heavy and unaddressed burden on European port communities and local economies.
  • It has been revealed that to quantify the cost of inaction, we evaluated at-berth emissions across the 100 largest EU ports using CE Delft’s Handbook on the External Costs of Transport.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How current shore power rules cost hundreds of millions every year in health and climate damages.

Air pollution and climate emissions from ships at berth impose a heavy and unaddressed burden on European port communities and local economies. While the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) took an vital first step by mandating Onshore Power Supply (OPS) for large container and passenger vessels, several blind spots leave over half of all in-port emissions unregulated.

It has been revealed that to quantify the cost of inaction, we evaluated at-berth emissions across the 100 largest EU ports using CE Delft’s Handbook on the External Costs of Transport. Based on 2024 MRV data, in-port emissions cost €2.53 billion every year in health damages and climate abatement costs. Covering only the electricity demand from large unregulated ship types would already save €500 million annually, while tackling boilers would save another €714 million. Shipping companies effectively offload these costs onto public budgets, making fossil fuels appear artificially cheap. Once all impacts are counted, using electricity when at berth is half as expensive as burning fossil fuels.

While AFIR successfully kickstarted early shore power roll-out, its narrow scope leaves significant volumes of emissions unaddressed. Beyond health and climate impacts, this partial coverage creates uncertainty and deprives port authorities, network operators , and investors from the predictability they need to develop and deploy the required infrastructure. Providing a clear time horizon for the provision of shore power to all ships is essential to share infrastructure costs, reduce electricity prices and permanently clean up air in ports.

By Eloi Nordé, Shipping Policy Officer, T&E.

Key insights from HPE’s Q4 earnings report

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1612 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Siliconangle

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.delivered a record fiscal fourth quarter this week, roughly doubling its fiscal 2027 growth outlook, but its stock gave back nearly all of the prior day’s rally.
  • Fourth-quarter revenue rose 50%, to $14.5 billion, orders grew 88%, and adjusted earnings of $1.43 per share topped the high end of guidance.
  • I joined a briefing with Chief Executive Antonio Neri and a small group of independent analysts shortly before the results came out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 15:27 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

ANALYSIS by Zeus Kerravala.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.delivered a record fiscal fourth quarter this week, roughly doubling its fiscal 2027 growth outlook, but its stock gave back nearly all of the prior day’s rally. The selloff suggests Wall Street still prices HPE as a low-margin server vendor, even though the results describe a networking and artificial intelligence infrastructure manufacturer with demand exceeding its ability to ship.

Fourth-quarter revenue rose 50%, to $14.5 billion, orders grew 88%, and adjusted earnings of $1.43 per share topped the high end of guidance. HPE now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 27% to 35%, with adjusted earnings of $5.05 to $5.35 per share, according to its earnings release.

I joined a briefing with Chief Executive Antonio Neri and a small group of independent analysts shortly before the results came out. Here are my four takeaways for investors and information technology leaders:.

Neri explained that networking orders grew more than 4.5 times faster than networking revenue in the quarter, up from 3.5 times the quarter before, and HPE exited the year with $10.5 billion in AI backlog.

HPE doubled its networking purchase commitments over the summer and raised them again in the fourth quarter, but those components carry lead times of 28 to 40-plus weeks, so Neri expects networking conversion to pick up starting in the second quarter. Supply constraints are a better problem to have than weak demand, but they mean fiscal 2027 hinges on converting orders rather than winning them.

The Juniper Networks integration is complete, and the annual cost-synergy target has risen to $800 million, but the bigger story remains the profit mix. Chief Financial Officer Marie Myers mentioned networking will account for more than 40% of HPE’s operating profit by the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, up from less than a quarter of revenue. AI is a major driver, with routing orders growing by triple digits as customers connect AI data centers to one another.

Security was the soft spot, which Neri called “just timing.” When I asked whether the security portfolio is where he wants it as the industry consolidates around substantial platforms, he argued for a different path.

Sources indicate that “Fortinet and we have a different strategy — the convergence of security and networking — and we are taking it all the way down to the silicon level,” he said. The convergence of networking and security is underway but will take time to execute, as a considerable amount of technical debt must go through its depreciation cycle. In a greenfield situation, organizations can easily deploy a converged solution, but in a brownfield environment, it requires much more work. This is the right strategy, but it remains a “prove-it” business for HPE.

Sources indicate that many neoclouds rely on vendor financing and chip-backed debt, raising real concerns about who is left exposed if the buildout slows. HPE indicates it has stayed out, and Neri was quite emphatic about it on the briefing.

“I want to be clear: We have not financed any neocloud through HPFS, our financing arm,” he remarked. “We have zero exposure to any AI financing for neocloud.” HPE has likely left some revenue on the table, but it drew the line in the right place. It will sell to neoclouds, as its $1.2 billion Vultr order shows, without acting as their bank. Enterprise and sovereign customers account for the majority of its cumulative AI orders, and if the neocloud financing chain breaks, HPE’s financing arm won’t be the one holding the paper.

Sources indicate that training built the first phase of AI infrastructure, and Neri believes inference will build the next and will dominate demand for AI infrastructure. “I believe by the end of the decade, 80% will be in AI inferencing,” he noted. “Much of that will land on-prem. Much of that will be distributed, for sure. That’s why the server business is structurally well-positioned.”.

Once agents are in production, token costs become a recurring bill, and companies will want inference running alongside their own data. Those servers require far more memory and pull in storage and services, which is better business than racking graphics processing units for a hyperscaler.

In a recent development, evidence of this is the interest in Helios, the Advanced Microdevices Inc. rack that uses HPE’s Ethernet switching rather than Nvidia’s proprietary interconnect. I asked Neri whether Jensen Huang’s brief departure from Nvidia Corp. had opened that door. He mentioned interest was building before then, as customers look to diversify.

Recent findings suggest that HPE shares jumped 17% on Monday ahead of the report as part of a broader AI rally, then fell about 13% in early trading on Tuesday, ending near where they started the week. I see three reasons for this.

Industry observers note that the first is margins. Cloud & AI operating margin was 18.4% in the quarter, and HPE guided to about 14% for fiscal 2027. Reuters reported that JPMorgan analysts called margin mix the key debate for investors.

The second is pricing. Myers said higher selling prices have been the biggest driver of server growth, and she expects gross margin to moderate in the second half as AI server volumes ramp and costs rise faster than pricing.

The third is timing. HPE expects about 54% of revenue in the second half, with the ramp tied to Helios shipments, the Oracle Corp. deal, customer data center readiness and component supply. Those are fair execution questions, but they miss the shift in where HPE’s profit comes from.

On the topic of margins, the 18.4% came off an unusual stretch of favorable pricing that should not have been modeled as permanent. Neri argued the guide is still “significantly higher than any historical margin we have had in this business,” and he’s right outside the past year. A year ago, the segment’s margin was 9.3%. Margin rate also isn’t margin dollars. At 30% to 40% revenue growth, my math shows Cloud & AI adding well over $1 billion in operating profit at the midpoint.

The bears are right that price-driven server growth doesn’t warrant a premium multiple, which is why the mix matters more. The market is fixated on the segment whose margins are normalizing and ignoring the one whose margins are expanding. Adjusted earnings per share are still guided to grow by 27% to 35%, in line with revenue growth. That’s far from the margin doom-and-gloom narrative on the stock.

The back-half concern is real but manageable. Myers described the pipeline as multiples of the backlog, and Neri noted the guide assumes only historical win rates against it.

In a recent development, then there’s quality. HPE is guiding to about 30% growth and at least $5.5 billion in free cash flow, has no neocloud financing exposure and has already brought leverage below its target. It trades at about eight times the midpoint of its adjusted earnings guidance. “I don’t see us at a multiple that is 8 to 9x; it makes no sense whatsoever,” Neri noted on the earnings call.

Sources indicate that for old HPE, that’s true, as it’s a server vendor, but HPE is increasingly a network vendor each quarter. In fact, during our pre-call with Neri, he led with networking and spoke at length about the business before pivoting to the server business. Expect networking to continue to drive a larger share of profits.

It has been revealed that fiscal 2027 is an execution year. HPE must convert purchase commitments into shipments, ramp Helios and prove that networking margins can climb even as cloud and AI margins settle. I’ll be watching networking order conversion more closely than server margins. If HPE executes, today’s multiple will prove to be too low.

Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

Sources indicate that as the wind energy industry matures, operators and service providers are increasingly focused on maximizing turbine availability while controlling long-term maintenance costs. Although major drivetrain components often receive the spotlight, one overlooked system can have an outsized impact on turbine reliability and performance: gearbox oil cooling.

It has been revealed that heat exchangers play a critical role in maintaining proper oil temperature and viscosity within wind turbine gearboxes. When cooling systems become clogged with airborne debris, dust, or organic material, oil temperatures rise, lubrication performance declines, and component stress increases. Over time, these conditions can contribute to reduced gearbox efficiency, elevated maintenance demands, and avoidable downtime.

“Wind operators today are balancing increasing performance expectations with the realities of aging fleets and rising maintenance costs. Technologies that improve cooling efficiency and reduce service exposure can have a meaningful impact on long-term turbine reliability and operational profitability,” according to Mike Erickson, HYDAC’s Market Manager for the Wind Industry.

Sources indicate that traditional “panel cut” heat exchanger designs have long been susceptible to clogging due to their tightly packed fin structures. In many wind environments — particularly agricultural, dusty, or high-pollen regions — debris accumulation can severely restrict airflow. Oil leaks can further compound the issue by trapping contaminants within the exchanger core, making cleaning more difficult and labor intensive.

This operational challenge has driven the need for more resilient cooling technologies designed specifically for real-world wind farm conditions.

Recent findings suggest that HYDAC’s upcoming “Square Wave” heat exchanger design represents a significant advancement in addressing these reliability concerns. Engineered to allow debris to pass more freely through the exchanger fins, the design minimizes clogging while improving cooling efficiency under demanding operating conditions.

It has been revealed that the importance of effective cooling cannot be overstated. Wind turbine gearbox oil typically operates within an optimal temperature range of approximately 45°C to 65°C. Even modest temperature increases can significantly impact oil viscosity. According to field data, a 12°C rise in oil temperature can reduce viscosity by nearly 28 percent — affecting lubrication quality and accelerating wear on critical drivetrain components.

Recent findings suggest that field trials have demonstrated measurable operational benefits from the Square Wave design. During a one-year trial on GE 1.x turbines, the upgraded exchanger consistently reduced clogging and lowered maintenance requirements compared to traditional panel cut cores. Operators reported reduced up-tower cleaning time and fewer temperature-related cooling faults.

Recent findings suggest that field validation across multiple turbine platforms has further reinforced the operational advantages of the Square Wave design. In one case study involving legacy 1 MW-class turbines operating in the Pacific Northwest, a major renewable energy operator installed pilot sets of Square Wave heat exchangers as part of a cooling performance evaluation. Installation teams reported the upgraded exchangers integrated seamlessly into the existing platform with no retrofit complications.

After initial operating data demonstrated improved cooling consistency, the operator expanded the evaluation program with additional units. Long-term SCADA analysis later showed turbines equipped with Square Wave technology operate approximately 20 to 25 percent cooler than comparable turbines using conventional heat exchanger designs under similar operating conditions. The data also highlighted another notable advantage: the Square Wave cores continued to maintain airflow and cooling efficiency in debris-heavy environments where traditional exchanger designs became increasingly restricted over time.

The successful deployment also generated interest from additional wind service organizations seeking retrofit-ready cooling upgrades that could improve turbine reliability while reducing maintenance burdens across aging fleets.

After two years of operation, turbines equipped with Square Wave heat exchangers operated approximately 19 to 25 percent cooler than reference turbines using standard exchanger designs under comparable operating conditions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that steel is considered the backbone of the American economy, critical for both national and economic security. It’s also the backbone of solar power construction, found commonly in the racking and mounting structures tilting solar panels toward the sun. And now, after years of tests and trials, an Ohio factory is roll-forming steel for a solar product that could use a stronger backbone — the solar panel.

A factory worker places a section of steel solar panel frames on a pallet in Welser Profile’s plant in Valley City, Ohio. Credit: Nextpower.

It has been revealed that roll-form steel company Welser Profile began manufacturing Nextpower’s NX CoreFrame steel panel frames earlier this year at its facility in Valley City, Ohio, just 30 miles outside Cleveland, and Solar Power World was invited to view production of its first major orders before adding another line fully dedicated to the solar component before the end of the year. Module frame company Origami Solar originally had the idea that swapping aluminum frames with steel would not only save the solar industry money and cut back on carbon emissions, it would also provide more physical support to bigger and heavier solar panels.

Welser, an Austrian firm with origins dating back to the 1660s, is a leader in roll-form steel profiles typically only seen in aluminum extrusions and helped produce a steel frame that’s easy for panel manufacturers to assemble and contractors to handle.

It has been revealed that “What’s special about Welser Profile is we pre-notch features in the material before it gets formed,” mentioned Bill Johnson, North America CEO of Welser Profile. “Everything about the solar industry is about how do we make it more efficient, cheaper, faster, better? You do that by all these little details to add value farther up the stream that minimizes labor, install cost. Our hole patterns and other features allow operators to snap things together, not bolt or weld things. Everyone is looking at how to make this work in a Lego setup, not a high-intense labor workforce installing all these panels.”.

According to recent reports, welser is helping bring the Origami Solar idea to life, but the upcoming owner of the tech, Nextpower, is delivering steel frames to the masses. Nextpower, a steel expert through its experience in producing tracking and mounting systems, acquired Origami in 2025 and will use its existing network of steel partners to convince more PV project developers to consider an alternative to aluminum.

According to recent reports, “Nextpower has debuted over 30 manufacturing facilities in the U.S. since 2020. Nextpower buys over 700,000 short tons of primary U.S. steel annually, which is more than a small car firm,” mentioned Jenya Meydbray, VP and general manager of Nextpower’s steel frames business. “Nextpower has had [the steel frame] for one year, building on the years of Origami’s engineering with Welser’s support. What we’re doing today is launching into high-scale, high-volume production here in Ohio.”.

The solar industry defaulted to aluminum panel frames because the material is lightweight, easy to handle and less susceptible to corrosion. But as the solar industry matured, more environmental and practical challenges became associated with the metal. Aluminum production on average has a five-times larger carbon footprint than steel production, a difficult point to ignore in the inherently green solar industry. Solar panels have also gotten larger in surface area and use less glass to cut weight. Aluminum might no longer be the ideal material to physically support these “substantial, floppy modules.”.

A steel coil feeds into a roll-forming machine producing solar panel frames. Credit: Nextpower.

It has been revealed that “Steel provides a far better structural support for the [panel] than aluminum does. That was the initial observation that the Origami founders made,” Meydbray stated. “They landed on this specific [roll-form] profile. Roll-forming is a precision process. We’re making millions of sticks of solar panel frames a month, and all of them have to be within sub-millimeter of precision across the full length. Welser is 100 years older than America, so Welser is definitely the most experienced in this art form of steel roll-forming.”.

In a recent development, welser set up North American operations in 2018 after acquiring an automotive roll-form operation in Valley City. The tech giant established a second location in the same industrial park to accommodate its growing client base in the solar, storage and energy industries.

Welser was one of the first roll-form partners to validate Magnelis — a zinc magnesium coating that has “self-healing” properties is capable of lasting 25 years in the field — and found it a great steel coating for solar energy applications. It’s one of the features of NX CoreFrame, Nextpower’s steel solar module frame.

Recent findings suggest that “Coming up with a newly introduced coating on steel, you don’t just throw it on the steel and sell it to the market. You have to trial it, validate it, make sure it works,” Johnson remarked. “Raw zinc — the coating has to be too thick for the longevity that the solar industry needs. Magnelis can go much lighter coating and still produce the same salt spray, same longevity, and it’s cheaper, faster, smarter.”.

Wesler is the latest high-volume production facility for NX CoreFrame, and Nextpower plans to reach 6.5 GW of annual production through additional manufacturing partners across the country.

In a recent development, with an established steel frame design, the product just needs to find a place on panel manufacturer’s production lines. Origami Solar had been signing supply agreements with U.S. panel assemblers, an activity that has only increased with the Nextpower transition. Meydbray said the pitch for a domestic supply chain has become more attractive, especially with Nextpower’s established regional steel manufacturing network.

In a recent development, A machine treats steel coil as it travels along a factory line. Credit: Nextpower.

Sources indicate that “Steel strengthens the supply chain of domestic manufacturing facilities. When frames are bought overseas, they spend five, six weeks on the water before they actually arrive to the factory. [Panel companies] have about 2,000 pallets of frames in inventory when they source from overseas,” he noted. “We’re able to provide actual just-in-time delivery to our factory clients. We can make deliveries every 48 hours. [They can save room] where they used to have pallets stacked up. There’s also the working capital of having stuff sit on the water for six weeks. Solar panel manufacturing is not a high-margin business, and working capital management is critical.”.

Nextpower has inked supply agreements with many multi-gigawatt panel manufacturers in the United States, including Jinko, T1 and Thornova.

According to recent reports, “This integration of Nextpower steel frames allows us to deliver high-performance modules tailored to the evolving U.S. market,” said Andrea Bodenhagen, global marketing director at Thornova Solar, which is establishing domestic solar cell manufacturing in Oklahoma. “By incorporating U.S.-made steel frames, we strengthen supply chain resilience while helping our customers maximize domestic content and improve project economics.”.

With bonus incentives from the investment tax credit still in play when solar projects use domestic products, an American-made steel frame can make all the difference.

Sources indicate that “When we see projects that have 100% domestic content on the tracker, we know that’s a perfect candidate for steel frames,” Meydbray remarked. “Steel frames get 6% domestic content credit. It’s the second cheapest percent after the tracker. A domestically made solar cell is a lot more expensive than an imported solar cell. The frame is the second-most cost-effective way to buy percentage points.”.

In a recent development, the NX CoreFrame is universal and can be used with any brand’s mounting or tracking system, but there are advantages when the project can be designed more cohesively through one supplier. Nextpower has spent the last year expanding beyond mounting systems, now offering inverter, electrical balance of system and panel products.

“[Nextpower] is ambitious, but it’s not arrogant. It prioritizes the customer relationships it’s built over the years. We spent time with our customers asking where their pain points are and expanded the business accordingly …  the tech giant that makes the thing the solar panel is mounted to is the same company that makes the frame that’s being mounted,” Meydbray said.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in-vehicle subscriptions are pretty universally maligned among car owners.
  • The new law, which takes effect on February 27, 2027, is part of a new section of the state's General Business Law, according to Spectrum News.
  • Hochul called the practice a "deceptive business model," according to CBS 6 Albany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in-vehicle subscriptions are pretty universally maligned among car owners. Most folks don't like the feeling of having to pay every month for features their cars were supposed to come with, and now Latest York State is doing something about it. Governor Kathy Hochul just signed a bill that bars automakers, dealers and their agents from selling subscriptions for features that are already installed.

The new law, which takes effect on February 27, 2027, is part of a new section of the state's General Business Law, according to Spectrum News. You can read the law for yourself here. It lays out fairly simple ground rules when it comes to subscriptions dealers or manufacturers can offer you: The feature must use hardware already in the car when it was bought or leased, and it must keep working without continual costs or support from the automaker or a third party. Those two things pretty much bring an end to crap like subscription-based heated seats and alike. It also is supposed to cover hands-off driving systems and enhanced navigation. Basically, once the hardware is physically in the car and the manufacturer isn't paying anything for you to use it, they can't then charge you. OEMs will also not be able to charge for software updates that fix safety defects.

Hochul called the practice a "deceptive business model," according to CBS 6 Albany. She also told automakers to keep their hands out of New Yorkers' wallets. It passed through the New York State Senate 57-3.

It has been revealed that as with all good things, there are some exceptions. First of all, your lease or payment strategy doesn't count as a subscription, so don't even try it, slick.

Recent findings suggest that the law also doesn't apply to navigation updates, infotainment features, satellite radio, in-vehicle WiFi, telematics, roadside assistance or "vehicle-connected services" that rely on cellular data or other networks, according to Motor1. It also exempts software-dependent driver assistance features, like Tesla's Full Self-Driving or GM's Super Cruise.

Industry observers note that I know what you're thinking. Didn't I just mention that hands-free driving systems are covered? Well, yes, but subscriptions tied to software and data are likely to survive, while hardware-only features are the real targets. Automakers will almost certainly make the argument that things like FSD and Super Cruise are "connected" or "software-dependent.".

Industry observers note that one prime example of what this bill aims to get rid of is BMW keeping things like a 360-degree camera behind a paywall. That hardware is already built into the car, and, as we reported, it doesn't require a data connection to operate. It's the same thing with features like high-beam assist and remote start, so I imagine it'll be hard for BMW and other companies with similar schemes to argue that these are "connected." I mean, these are the same people who argue that buyers actually want subscriptions, which is certainly not true.

In any case, violators will face civil penalties of up to $250 per point-of-sale for each violation, though it's not clear exactly how that'll be counted. It's not clear if other states are going to follow suit, but here's hoping.

In a recent development, the Sienna's new hybrid powertrain has been totally recalibrated to operate the 2.5-liter four-cylinder at lower engine speeds when accelerating through the low and mid-range, and all Siennas now have a 1.15-kWh lithium-ion battery and a 166-horsepower electric motor. The powertrain produces a combined 251 horsepower, 6 more horses than last year, and Toyota reckons it's good for a 0.3-second quicker 0-to-60 sprint of 7.5 seconds in front-wheel-drive form. It can still be had with all-wheel drive, which adds a rear-mounted 54-hp electric motor, but its 0-to-60 time is actually a tenth slower than the front-drive model. Toyota now estimates both FWD and AWD Siennas will return 39 mpg in the city, 35 mpg on the highway, and 37 mpg combined, improvements of 3 mpg for FWD and 4 mpg for AWD.

Toyota indicates the latest steering system is more direct and has better on-center feel while reducing steering effort at low speeds for easier parking thanks to a new steering gear box, motor control unit, and torque sensor. The Sienna's brakes have also been reworked with a new electronic control system, offering improved feel and response with less body roll. The latest Toyota Safety Sense 4.0 suite of active safety features has upgraded sensors and hardware for improved obstacle detection capabilities, and in case that all fails, a built-in dash cam comes standard.

In a recent development, other little changes include the cancellation of the Limited model, now leaving base LE, XLE, Woodland, XSE, and top Platinum trim levels. Toyota has not yet release pricing for the updated 2027 Sienna, but we expect its prices to increase slightly from their current starting point of $42,915.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With how ubiquitous commercial air travel is today it's easy to overlook how astonishingly rapid early aircraft development was. There were only 24 years between the maiden flight of the Wright Flyer in 1903 and Charles Lindbergh made the first solo transatlantic flight in 1927. However, military thinkers were even quicker to realize the potential of powered flight on the battlefield. The U.S. Army purchased a Wright Military Flyer in 1909 for use as an observation aircraft. The first heavier-than-air military aircraft served as the spark that eventually led to creation of the U.S. Air Force, but it wasn't an unmitigated success.

Sources indicate that the tactical advantage of holding the higher ground had been known for centuries, but aircraft opened up an entirely upcoming dimension. Initially, it was hot air balloons taking to the wild blue yonder. During the Civil War, the Union Army fielded a balloon corps to perform reconnaissance and scout Confederate Army positions. The corps wouldn't last long with then-General Ulysses S. Grant dissolving the unit in August 1863.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Army decided to revive this reconnaissance role when opening bidding for a two-seat observation aircraft in 1908. According to the U.S. Department of Defense, the Wright Military Flyer reached an altitude of 400 feet while averaging a speed of 42.5 miles per hour during its final ten-mile qualifying flight in July 1909. The service would purchase a single Wright Military Flyer for $30,000 next month. The sum would be $1.1 million today when adjusted for inflation.

The demonstration campaign that convinced the U.S. Army Signal Corps to open its checkbooks wasn't flawless. Orville Wright would bring a Wright Model A plane to Fort Myer near Arlington National Cemetery in 1908. The younger Wright brother flew dignitaries on brief flights around the Fort's drilling grounds in front of over 2,000 people.

The spectacle was going perfectly until First Lieutenant Thomas Selfridge climbed abroad as a passenger. He had been the first U.S. Army officer to fly a plane just months earlier. According to Air & Space Magazine, Model A suffered a propeller failure while flying at 40 mph at an altitude of at least 100 feet. The twin-propeller wood and canvas biplane tumbled out of control and plummeted to the ground. Wright was seriously injured, but the crash killed Selfridge.

In the crash's aftermath, a distraught Wright believed that he could've landed the plane safely if he had "a few feet more" of altitude. He returned to Fort Myer with an upgraded plane the next year and secured the sale to the Signal Corps. The Wright Military Flyer would never see combat, but it's easy to see how the early aircraft would've been vulnerable to machine gun fire from the ground with such a low maximum altitude. It wouldn't be the U.S. Army's last foray into experimental aircraft. The service would dabble in early drone warfare less than a decade later.

Let's ground your enthusiasm just a tad here. Consumer Reports (CR) just came out with a list of a dozen 2026 models that at the moment offer steep Black Friday discounts. The organization is highlighting these deals because every whip on its list also received a strong overall score in Consumer Reports' testing. We have our own take on which vehicles we'd chase hardest, however, so we'll edit CR's edit.

Recent findings suggest that to square up that giant publisher's musts, the vehicles are weighed on factors like how they perform on the site's road tests. And to earn a higher rating, cars that CR recommends need to have performed well in the owner surveys it conducts on hundreds of thousands of cars — the organization wants its readers to consider whether they'd buy the same car again if they had the chance. It also prefers vehicles that get better marks from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS).

Recent findings suggest that consumer Reports also gives higher ratings for standard active safety tech. This includes automatic emergency braking, blind-spot warning systems, and rear cross-traffic warning systems. And the publication gives props to vehicles that come with camera systems that monitor the driver for attentiveness. The outlet layers on extra credit if the IIHS notes a car does well in its front crash protection tests for pedestrians. Consumer Reports' recommended rating also comes down to predicted reliability, again based on reader surveys.

Still, we've got our own take here, and we do a deeper dive on the discount fine print as well as sift their dozen choices down to an odd five cars — just because a car's cheaper doesn't mean you want it in the driveway for the next decade.

Industry observers note that the American-made Honda Ridgeline qualifies for some hefty incentives. Consumer Reports found discounts equaling up to $4,953. That's probably due to varied incentives offered by different dealers. For example, you can find $2,250 off via a national incentive directly from Honda, while Carsdirect shows up to $2,750 off and 1.99% financing for 36 months. While a three-year loan means paying more per month than a longer term, 1.99% is far lower than the latest national average rate of 7.3% — meaning you'd be spending far less to pay off your Honda.

Recent findings suggest that poke around at area dealers, too. We found a deal offering at least $3,045 off of the Ridgeline, which actually exceeds the deal tallied by Consumer Reports, courtesy of Friendly Honda in Newly introduced York's Hudson Valley. There's another way to save on the Ridgeline after you make the purchase. See, the truck is listed on Consumer Reports' top USA-made cars list, which could unlock some major loan deductions. The way that works is that if you purchase a qualifying American-made vehicle, the IRS gives you a tax credit of up to $10,000 on the interest paid on the loan for that new truck. On the Ridgeline, we arrived at a $5,633 in deductions.

Even without the tax credit, getting several thousand bucks off the Ridgeline makes it extra compelling. We praised its handling in our review of the off-road-focused Honda Ridgeline Trailsport, and we dig its ride quality. Ford's Maverick didn't make Consumer Reports' best cars made in America list, but this Honda wins for that, and we like it for out-towing the Ford, too.

Earlier this year, we put the Hyundai Elantra on our list of the cheapest new cars on the market for 2026. You, dear reader, also voted the Elantra onto your list of the best value cars, too. Consumer Reports found potential deals of up to $2,958 off the Elantra SEL's $23,950 MSRP before destination costs. Our own research demonstrates $2,000 back from Hyundai nationally, while some individual dealers such as Danbury Hyundai in Connecticut have an additional $500 available for recent college graduates and another $500 for first responders.

As for why you like it — you actually prefer the Elantra Hybrid. The bummer there is that there's only a $500 discount off the $26,650 base price of that more fuel-efficient version of the Elantra. We get the thinking: We praised the Hybrid for being quieter and riding better than the non-hybrid, but don't forget that the base SE runs $24,120 with destination, before the $2,000 discount.

According to recent reports, previously, we praised the standard feature set, including an 8.0-inch touchscreen display, the fact that it gets standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and of course, Consumer Reports likes that it also comes baked with a blind-spot warning system, rear cross-traffic warning, and automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, as well as lane keeping. Oh, and if you're lanky, the Elantra easily fits taller drivers thanks to 40.6 inches of headroom and 42.3 inches of legroom.

According to recent reports, we don't know how Hyundai will price the next-generation Elantra – which feels too nice to be treated like an economy car. That may mean it won't be as affordable come this time next year, so you should probably buy one now, before prices climb.

It has been revealed that consumer Reports found savings of $4,852 off the 2026 Santa Fe. We found that Hyundai is offering a $3,000 national program plus 0% interest loans for up to 60 months, which is a very good way to save a lot of money on the carrying costs of a latest car. Look around for other dealer incentives, too. We also found another $2,004 off offered by Ontario Hyundai in the Los Angeles area, knocking nearly $5,000 off the Santa Fe SEL's $40,075 sticker.

We dig the Santa Fe for lots of reasons. Back in 2024, we called it boxy and beautiful from every angle and praised Hyundai for moving from its frumpy curves to a more chiseled bod. Then there's the combination of utility — since it seats up to seven humans — and the fact that the interior is well designed and comfortable. We crowned it the crossover to end all crossovers, too, in part because we really love the dual-clutch transmission and the Santa Fe's superb ride.

Recent findings suggest that if you're instead chasing fuel economy, Hyundai's $3,000 off the 2026 Santa Fe Hybrid is a better price cut than the carmaker's offering for the Elantra Hybrid. At $40,380, the 2026 Santa Fe Hybrid still pulls a major premium over the non-hybrid, but you can qualify for the same 0% interest loan for 60 months.

Recent findings suggest that audi's A3 and S3 are cars we can't help but drool over. That's partly because they're sports sedans, which is a dying breed. Audi is right now offering up to $3,500 off the sticker price of the A4 and $2,500 off the S3. That nudges the $41,495 A3's sticker (after destination) just beneath $40,000. However, the $53,395 S3 only gets a minor haircut.

We noted back in 2025, when the Audi A3 and S3 underwent their most recent refresh, that that the cars are really petite — about three inches shorter than the Honda Civic. And yet we claimed that the Audi S3 is all the car you'll ever need. Our review of the S3 dovetails with why Consumer Reports likes the lower-tier A3, saying it outperforms peers like the BMW 2 Series Gran Coupe and Mercedes-Benz CLA. A base, 201-horsepower inline-four provides reasonable power in the A3, and while Consumer Reports doesn't love the car's dual-clutch transmission, we found this seven-speed gearbox delightful.

Note that this is a driver's car, first. We praised the driver's seat for its support, and so did Consumer Reports — but they handed a demerit to the squished nature of the rear perches. Did we mention it's smaller than a Honda Civic?

It has been revealed that you can get up to $4,500 off the Rogue Platinum and $3,500 off lower-tier Rogues, but hunt a bit. We found $3,000 off a Rogue SV with a national incentive, plus another $950 from Poughkeepsie Nissan in Fresh York. That knocked the total sticker down to $31,235. Then again, at a different dealer in Los Angeles, prices are sliding $3,000 across the table alongside $3,500 from Nissan, which drops the sticker of a Rogue SV from $32,500 down to $26,122. Even if you don't live in L.A., maybe it's worth flying out to buy that Nissan.

Sources indicate that as for the Rogue's attributes, they're good, if not revolutionary. The new-for-2027 Rogue Hybrid, however, is a total game-changer thanks to an entirely reinvented hybrid system, where we said its silence speaks volumes, because it operates way more like a pure EV. That said, the 1.5-liter turbocharged inline-three beneath the hood of the 2026 Rogue is still plenty punchy, with 201 hp. Key to that sensation is low-end torque of 225 pound-feet hitting at 2,800 rpm and sticking around through 4,000 rpm.

We noted that the Nissan's inline-3 delivers power more like what you'd expect from a larger V6, but the bonus is you're not pushing all those extra pistons. That means the FWD Rogue gets a combined 32 mpg while the AWD model gets 31 mpg. That's not the 38 mpg Nissan expects from its latest Rogue Hybrid, but if you can nab a 2026 Rogue for $26,000 versus the $37,065 tab on that latest-and-greatest Nissan, we're guessing you'll be just fine with that trade-off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 16:12 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are criticizing Nvidia Corp.’s decision to rehire Jensen Huang as its chief executive.

According to recent reports, the criticism came against the backdrop of a controversial move by the U.S. Commerce Department. The agency applied new export restrictions to Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud operator. The company played a prominent role in the spy controversy that led to Huang’s resignation. According to trade experts, the Commerce Department left out a key clause that is usually included in such restrictions.

Recent findings suggest that huang resigned on Nov. 12 following revelations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. Early reporting about the relationship indicated that she was found to have passed intelligence to China. The U.S. Justice Department later stated that it has not yet reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang is a spy. Earlier this week, the Newly introduced York Times reported that she maintained contact with a Chinese intelligence official.

In a recent development, nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang on Monday after U.S. President Donald Trump and tech industry figures urged directors to bring him back. The move drew widespread criticism from members of Congress.

Sources indicate that house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-Upcoming York), who is set to become House Speaker, called the reinstatement “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.” Rep. Don Bacon (R-Nebraska), the chair of House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies and Innovation, said that “it’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO.” Former Utah Republican Senator and Massachusetts Governor Mitt Romney tweeted: “Let me get this straight: we rushed AI along without regulating safeguards in order to stay ahead of China and at the same time, we sold China the very chips they’d need to get ahead of us. Smells of profit, corruption and perhaps worse.”.

Sources indicate that multiple lawmakers told CNBC that they plan to scrutinize Huang’s conduct closely. The executive is scheduled to testify before multiple Congressional committees next Tuesday. Furthermore, Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Oregon) told the outlet that Democrats plan to scrutinize the Trump administration’s role in the matter.

It has been revealed that the Commerce Department today added Megaspeed and several of its regional affiliates to its Entity List. Companies on the list can only purchase sensitive products such as graphics cards if they obtain a license from the U.S. government. According to Gizmodo, the move has drawn scrutiny because the restrictions applied to Megaspeed include a loophole.

Recent findings suggest that all the companies on the Entity List are prohibited from buying Nvidia’s latest chips unless they secure a license. Most of them are also unable to buy lower-end graphics cards, high-bandwidth memory and related hardware. The latter restrictions are specified in a clause called the FDPR provision. The Commerce Department has reportedly not applied the FDPR provision to Megaspeed when it added the firm to the Entity List.

Recent findings suggest that huang returned to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters on Monday. The news sent the chipmaker’s stock soaring more than 30%, although it parred some of the gains today. Nvidia shares are down 5.8% from Monday.

Wired today published excerpts from Huang’s all-hands meeting with employees. The executive apologized for his affairs and for his management style, which has also come under scrutiny in recent days. He added that he will undergo a “360-degree review” and that Nvidia’s code of conduct is still in effect.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Before you get too excited, Ford is not exactly taking over the space business, nor is it necessarily competing against SpaceX.
  • Alongside its newly minted minority ownership status, the automaker will apply its manufacturing experience to help kickstart Revolution’s spacecraft platform into volume production.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Intertubes are practically bursting at the seam with news of another step towards the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, both of which are helmed by on-again, off-again Trump supporter Elon Musk. Buried beneath the avalanche of press is another automotive-aerospace mashup, that being Ford Motor Tech giant’s newly confirmed investment in the US startup Revolution Space. Evidently the iconic automaker is particularly interested in Revolution’s “unique in-space propulsion technologies.” Hmmm…interesting!

Before you get too excited, Ford is not exactly taking over the space business, nor is it necessarily competing against SpaceX. Revolution specializes in spacecraft, not rocket launches. In addition, Ford is not merging itself with Revolution. On November 23, Ford revealed that it is taking up a minority stake in the startup for a yet-to-be-disclosed sum, through its Industrial Platform LLC subsidiary.

Alongside its newly minted minority ownership status, the automaker will apply its manufacturing experience to help kickstart Revolution’s spacecraft platform into volume production.

It has been revealed that so, what does Ford have that Revolution wants? Apparently, lots. “With Ford’s manufacturing capabilities, the companies are partnering to industrialize Revolution Space’s next-generation spacecraft at scale, unlocking latest dynamic missions and proliferated constellations,” Ford explained in a press statement.

Ford’s Chief Strategy Officer, Marin Gjaja, also chipped in his two cents, emphasizing that “Ford’s strength is building complex products in large volumes, something today’s growing satellite market requires.”.

Gjaja also underscored Ford’s immediate interest in the matter, which is to diversify and harden itself against the shifting winds of the global auto market — presumably including the abrupt shift in federal energy policy here in the US, too. As cited by Ford, the “space economy” right now registers about $600 billion globally, which is peanuts compared to the $1.8 trillion anticipated by 2035.

“Increasingly scaled satellite manufacturing is one of the drivers of that growth,” Ford further explains, noting that the firm Future Market Insights estimates the global satellite manufacturing market in the range of $87–$114 billion by 2035, heads and shoulders above the current estimate of $22–$26 billion.

If all goes according to plan, Revolution Space will give the automaker a hand in government and commercial satellite applications. Ford lists communications, Earth observation, navigation, space domain awareness, satellite servicing, and scientific and deep-space missions among the areas of interest. One can  safely assume that military applications are in there somewhere, too.

As for what Ford may expect in return in terms of technology transfer, that remains to be seen. Ford notes that its experience in the aerospace field includes building communications and weather satellites for NASA and the military here in the US, as well as NATO.

According to recent reports, however, that work goes back 50-60 years ago. The satellites of today are a different creature. “Revolution Space delivers and operates advanced space systems with superior performance and propulsion technologies designed to achieve the precision control and sustained maneuverability to enhance existing and create new, high-value, dynamic missions,” Ford notes.

In the November 24 announcement, Ford also notes that it has deployed its manufacturing experience to pivot into newly introduced fields as called for, citing the bombers it built during World War II and, more recently, the ventilators and protective equipment it supplied during the outset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

According to recent reports, drones could be next on the menu. Coincidentally or not, on November 24, the Wall Street Journal reported that Ford is in the running to help supply drones to the Department of Defense, alongside General Motors among other stakeholders. If realized, the program would call for supplying actuators, engines, sensors, lidar and other elements to drone manufacturers.

“Defense Department leaders have spent months enlisting automakers and their well-established supply chains to help scale up production of everything from missiles to tactical trucks. Now, they want those companies to help ease shortages of unmanned systems, including surveillance and strike drones, that have become crucial in global conflicts,” WSJ elaborated.

Good luck with that. Don’t expect anything of consequence to materialize until Defense Secretary Pete Hesgeth leaves office, either voluntarily or by virtue of impeachment over the hash he has made of the Defense Department, including its equipment as well as its personnel.

According to recent reports, still, the WSJ report did yield an interesting nugget about Ford’s minority stake in Revolution Space. For those without a subscription, the Detroit Free Press kindly offers a summary citing Ford spokesperson David Tovar, who noted that Ford has “had discussions with the Pentagon” focusing on its recent investment in Revolution Space, as well as the manufacture of vehicles for the military.

In a recent development, that’s a good question. The Revolution website is rather thin on the technology itself, though it does note that the board is chaired by former NASA administrator Daniel Goldin, with former NASA astronaut Paul W. Richards serving as Chief Engineer and Chief Strategy Officer.

It has been revealed that revolution does drop a few hints about its expectations for the manufacturing hookup with Ford. The company notes that in 2025 it was selected for the DARPA “LASSO” program, with DARPA being short for the Defense Advanced Research Agency.

DARPA describes LASSO as a program aimed at “significantly increasing the United States’ ability to conduct operations in support of space situational awareness by developing both autonomous satellite navigation in stressing orbital conditions and increasing satellite maneuverability through continuous dynamic repositioning based on changing conditions, with the added benefit of creating a proven reserve model for resources relevant to ISRU on Earth’s Moon,” with ISRU being short for in-situ resource utilization.

In a recent development, if you guessed water on the moon is the aim, run right out and buy yourself a cigar. “The program seeks performers to design, test, build, and deliver a spacecraft capable of determining all areas on the Moon that contain greater than 5% water concentration,” DARPA explains.

The LASSO selection comes on the heels of a flurry of activity in 2024, when Revolution reported that it was awarded a slot in the “Advanced Capabilities & Demonstration Missions” program of the Defense Innovation Unit. DIU also deployed its fast-track authority under the “Other Transactions” program to tap Revolution for an award in support of the organization’s responsive modular electrospray thrust technology.

In 2024 Revolution Space also reported that it earned an award from the Defense Department’s “Accelerate the Procurement and Fielding of Innovative Technologies” program, and it nailed down an agreement with NASA to collaborate on space technology.

As for the Tesla-SpaceX merger, if you have any thoughts about that drop a note in the comment thread.

From Key Cloning To Car Trackers: How 'GTA 6' Is Making Car Theft A Bigger Hassle

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like missions and side quests, stealing cars has always been an integral part of the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise.
  • Industry observers note that while you can still do things the old-fashioned way, like pulling the driver out and taking control of the vehicle, or smashing a window, hotwiring the car, and driving away, those methods won't necessarily work on every car across the fictional state of Leonida.
  • According to recent reports, how can you tell if a car is keyless or has a tracker installed?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like missions and side quests, stealing cars has always been an integral part of the "Grand Theft Auto" franchise. For "GTA 6," not only have the developers leaned into advanced physics for more realistic car crashes, but car theft itself has evolved into multiple tiers.

Industry observers note that while you can still do things the old-fashioned way, like pulling the driver out and taking control of the vehicle, or smashing a window, hotwiring the car, and driving away, those methods won't necessarily work on every car across the fictional state of Leonida. For example, keyless cars can't be hotwired. Even if someone left the doors of their expensive sports car open, you can't simply waltz in and drive away without a key cloner, which you'll only get access to later in the game. Standard and advanced vehicle trackers are also something to keep in mind. (Minor progression spoilers ahead.).

According to recent reports, how can you tell if a car is keyless or has a tracker installed? Enter the WAiNK app. Your friend Cal installs it on your phone during a story mission in Chapter 1. The app lets you scan a car to see its make and model and whether it's locked, alarmed, keyless, or fitted with a tracker. Additionally, the app tells you the car's condition, how much it's worth, and what it costs to register should you wish to own it. Keep in mind that although registering stolen cars is how you take ownership of them in "GTA 6," that feature won't be unlocked until Chapter 2, when you meet Moses, who gifts you a slim jim.

To steal cars without breaking the window or setting off the alarm, you'll need to use a slim jim. It works through a lock-picking minigame when you interact with a locked, unoccupied vehicle. While the method is unlikely to attract unwanted attention, it still won't let you start cars with keyless ignition. For that, you'll need to wait until you're about halfway through Chapter 3, at which point you'll get a key cloner. (It's a phone app you download during a story mission.).

The process itself is similar to using the slim jim, and once it's done, the door unlocks, and you drive away — no need to hotwire the car. As mentioned earlier, you can use the WAiNK app before you try to steal a car to see which sort of tracker it has, among other details. Standard trackers are not that major of a deal — the catch is that you can't take the car to a mod shop for any kind of modifications unless you've registered it as your own.

Cars with advanced trackers, on the other hand, alert the police and pinpoint your location — remember, "GTA 6" has flock-like cameras to track your movements. You'll have to drive really fast to stop the tracker from sending the location signal to the cops. If you slow down, the tracker starts beeping, and you only have a few seconds to speed up before it gives away your location. And, unlike in older "GTA" games, cars in "GTA 6" don't have infinite gas, so keep that in mind as well.

R-Line with two output levels. The ID. Cross R-Line will be released initially with 99 kW (135 PS) and a 37 kWh battery. The entry-level version already offers extensive R-Line standard equipment: this includes a bumper in R-Line design, vertical daytime headlights, 19-inch alloy wheels and anthracite-coloured exterior mirror covers. A side application with R-Line lettering sets an additional accent. In the interior, sports comfort seats in the specific R-Line trim underline the car’s dynamic character. The interactive ID. Light, which extends into the front doors, is also on board as standard. The extensive standard equipment also includes Keyless Access (for keyless opening and starting of the vehicle), background lighting, IQ.LIGHT (with LED matrix headlights and striking light signature) and numerous assist systems. For example, the rear-view camera simplifies manoeuvring, while adaptive cruise control (ACC) automatically maintains the set distance to the vehicle in front. The standard-equipment progressive steering also combines direct handling when manoeuvring with precise steering characteristics at higher speeds. Prices for the 99 kW (135 PS) version start at 37,225 euros.

Cross R-Line is particularly dynamic when combined with the larger 52 kWh battery: the output increases to 166 kW (226 PS) and the maximum torque is up to 290 Nm. This means that the ID. Cross R-Line accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 6.9 seconds and reaches a top speed of 175 km/h. The 52 kWh battery enables a WLTP range of up to 428 kilometres. Pre-sales of this most powerful version will start in the second half of March 2027.

Recent findings suggest that more agility and traction. In addition to the higher performance, the top-of-the-range model differs from the entry-level version above all due to its specially tuned chassis technology. The electronically controlled front differential lock, DCC adaptive chassis control including (lowered by 15 mm) and progressive steering are on board as standard. The front differential lock improves traction, driving stability and steering behaviour, while DCC continuously adapts damping to the road surface and driving situation. The progressive steering ensures more direct steering and at the same time makes manoeuvring easier. In addition, a vehicle dynamics manager integrates the central chassis systems with each other. The top-of-the-range model thus combines agility and safe traction with high ride comfort.

Exclusive Traction driving profile. The new Traction driving profile is also exclusive to the 166 kW version. It supplements the Eco, Comfort, Sport and Individual programs and specifically adjusts the drive and front differential lock to slippery road surfaces or roads with varying grip. Drivers benefit from harmonious power transmission and additional traction, especially in wet and wintry conditions.

Sources indicate that sportiness meets everyday life. The ID. Cross combines driving dynamics with plenty of space and flexibility. A luggage compartment volume of 475 litres and a frunk with an additional 25 litres offer plenty of space for travel, leisure and luggage. The 52 kWh battery versions are also available with a ball coupling (optional) for a towing capacity of up to 1,200 kg. With a drawbar load of 75 kilograms, two e-bikes can also be transported, for example.

Tesla Wants You To Watch Its 'Reality View' Instead Of Paying Attention To Reality

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (390 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Jalopnik

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there's little Tesla loves more than a dumb little party trick, and it often includes latest gimmick functionality within major updates to its software.
  • Industry observers note that the Tesla faithful call the software upgrade V15, after the FSD version included, but the full package is known as Update 2026.38.6.11 — not exactly a name that rolls off the tongue.
  • FSD 15 can see chain link fence and power lines!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there's little Tesla loves more than a dumb little party trick, and it often includes latest gimmick functionality within major updates to its software. The recent release of V15, software for Tesla's latest in-car computers, adds another trick: A new camera angle that highlights the car from a third-person view, like in a video game. Tesla calls it Reality View, and out of everything a Tesla can do, it sure is one of the things.

Industry observers note that the Tesla faithful call the software upgrade V15, after the FSD version included, but the full package is known as Update 2026.38.6.11 — not exactly a name that rolls off the tongue. The update did include functional changes to FSD, mostly relating to the computer vision wall Tesla keeps beating its head against, but it seems the engineers had a thought while working on all those cameras: Why not use them to simulate a third-person view, like a video game?

FSD 15 can see chain link fence and power lines! 🤯🙌🏽 @Tesla @TeslaSI @elonmusk pic.twitter.com/m3fn7c4obA.

It has been revealed that initially, after looking at both Tesla's demo footage and footage from real owners, I figured the car was using SpaceXAI's models to generate a third-person view based on the input from the cameras — a method that would explain some of the odd glitches and scale challenges present in some of the clips as AI hallucinations. According to Elon Musk's tweets, that's exactly what's going on — rather than an actual display of what the car's cameras and FSD software see, Tesla owners are now treated to an AI-generated picture of what's going on around them.

Recent findings suggest that the ability to mesh multiple cameras into a single point of view like this is neat, and the underlying tech is impressive, though it's unclear how much compute is needed to generate these images, and what kind of load that puts on the car. What these images aren't, though, are replacements for the actual data visualization that FSD used to supply. Even Tesla owners are admitting confusion between objects the car does and doesn't see with the new display. Most Tesla party tricks are some ratio of neat to useless, but this one genuinely appears to make the user experience of FSD worse.

#122317. Breaking: Europe’s Inland Shipping Models Underprice Green Fuels. Market Prices Favor Battery Swapping.

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (927 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cleantechnica ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Europe’s Inland Shipping Models Underprice Green Fuels. Market Prices Favor Battery Swapping.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (927 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cleantechnica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that europe’s inland-shipping models underprice renewable diesel.
  • In a recent development, the gap between the modeled HVO price and observed market prices matters for the investment choices these studies inform.
  • The Central Commission for the Navigation of the Rhine (CCNR) commissioned the original transition study behind its 2021 roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that europe’s inland-shipping models underprice renewable diesel. For a upcoming 110-meter dry-cargo vessel, PLATINA4Action calculates HVO (hydrotreated vegetable oil) propulsion at €1,798/day against €1,964/day for battery swapping. Apply the observed October 2026 Dutch HVO market price, including delivery, and the HVO cost is €2,515/day. Battery swapping is €551/day cheaper. The model’s claim of an HVO cost advantage fails a market-price check.

In a recent development, the gap between the modeled HVO price and observed market prices matters for the investment choices these studies inform. It also exposes a wider pattern. European studies give renewable liquid fuels favorable future prices while expecting marine batteries to remain expensive for much longer than the broader battery market suggests.

The Central Commission for the Navigation of the Rhine (CCNR) commissioned the original transition study behind its 2021 roadmap. Its scenarios influenced subsequent work, including the EU-linked PLATINA4Action and SYNERGETICS projects. Those projects do not all use identical models, but their assumptions and recommendations contribute to a shared policy picture in which several combustion pathways are expected to remain competitive with direct electrification.

In a recent development, in the full TFIE assessment, I converted the October 2026 Dutch Class II HVO wholesale benchmark, added a delivery allowance and expressed the result in 2025 euros. The market-based HVO cost is €2.59/kg. Battery swapping becomes cheaper than HVO in the PLATINA4Action 110-meter vessel comparison at approximately €1.93/kg. At that observed market price, modeled HVO propulsion costs €2,515/day over the model’s 2028–2047 ownership period, against €1,964/day for swapping. The model puts fossil diesel at €1,844/day, leaving swapping about 7% above diesel but 22% below market-priced HVO.

It has been revealed that the price difference matters to freight operators. CCNR’s 2026 cost indices allocate fuel 35% of dry-bulk costs, 30% of tanker costs and 28% of container shipping costs. Operators compete for cargo against rivals still burning diesel. Expensive alternative fuels cannot be passed through to customers merely because a transition scenario requires them.

Sources indicate that an April 2025 statement from European inland shipping and port organizations called for enough HVO at diesel-competitive prices to supply 1.6 million tons annually by around 2030. That quantity roughly matches the sector’s entire conventional diesel consumption in 2015. It exceeds the EU’s 2025 sustainable aviation fuel supply of 1.1 million tons by about 45%.

HVO and conventional biodiesel compete for oils and fats also used to produce aviation fuel. Aviation has fewer practical routes to electrification, and its European mandates create demand for renewable kerosene. An HVO-centered inland strategy puts barges in direct competition with aircraft for constrained feedstocks, even where barges can draw electricity from a corridor network.

Synthetic fuels present an even sharper problem. SYNERGETICS gives green methanol from biological and synthetic routes a combined low wholesale price of €350/t in its stated-policy case from 2035. That same scenario uses a low green-hydrogen price of €3.50/kg. Producing a ton of synthetic methanol takes about 190 kilograms of hydrogen, costing €665 before carbon dioxide, synthesis, financing and delivery. The hydrogen input alone costs almost twice the assumed low finished-fuel price.

It has been revealed that biomethanol is a different production route. It can be made from agricultural and forestry residues, and I expect it to play a useful role in deep-sea shipping. Grouping biological and synthetic methanol together conceals the economics of each. For inland waterways, the relevant competitor is often electricity delivered directly to the propeller, not fossil methanol replaced with greener methanol.

The battery forecasts lean in the opposite direction. SYNERGETICS places 2030 marine battery storage at €210–€520/kWh, a €365 midpoint. My inland freight electrification report models standardized marine battery containers at €100/kWh in 2030, including the marine safety and container systems, with vessel integration costed separately. A €265/kWh difference adds €1.06 million to a 4 MWh battery installation before operating the vessel. The full fleet-level analysis also prices spare batteries, financing, charging infrastructure and equipment held in reserve.

It has been revealed that the studies’ fleet assumptions compound the fuel-price choices. One PLATINA4Action case requires a large Rhine or Danube pusher to go seven days without replenishing energy, excluding intermediate charging or exchange from the test. The SYNERGETICS SYNFEED model starts every new vessel with a Stage V combustion engine, leaving electrification to later retrofits. Those are consequential design choices for a transition modeled through 2050.

Sources indicate that freight demand should be modeled before fuel demand. Mineral oil products, coal and iron ore accounted for 35.7% of Rhine cargo mass in 2025. CCNR’s own underlying economic projections point toward large declines in coal, refining and primary metals, even as construction and trade grow. The amount and composition of freight needing propulsion in 2050 will differ from today’s cargo mix.

The Netherlands has already reduced its 2040 hydrogen demand expectations and identified electricity as the main inland-shipping pathway toward 2050. CCNR is revisiting its transition work. The upcoming analysis should start with the freight that will actually move, calculate route energy and charging or exchange needs, and then test the remaining fuel demand against prices reflecting aviation, deep-sea shipping and industrial competition.

Sources indicate that technology neutrality is a method of comparing alternatives, not an obligation to finance every fuel pathway. With HVO priced against market evidence and batteries costed realistically, the investment case for parallel fuel infrastructure weakens.

According to recent reports, the full TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment walks through the CCNR, PLATINA4Action and SYNERGETICS cost assumptions, the HVO crossover and the synthetic-fuel arithmetic. The open inland freight electrification report contains the route, fleet and infrastructure model.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, shares of human resources and finance software manufacturer Workday Inc.
  • In a recent development, for the quarter that ended on Oct.
  • Subscription revenue rose 12.8% from a year earlier, to $2.532 billion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATED 17:27 EST / NOVEMBER 24 2026.

According to recent reports, shares of human resources and finance software manufacturer Workday Inc. fell more than 7% in late trading today after a softer-than-expected subscription revenue forecast for the current quarter overshadowed fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue that came in ahead of Wall Street’s targets.

In a recent development, for the quarter that ended on Oct. 31, Workday reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.82, up 22% from $2.32 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $2.705 billion, up 11.2% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting earnings of $2.75 per share on revenue of $2.69 billion.

Subscription revenue rose 12.8% from a year earlier, to $2.532 billion. Net income on an unadjusted basis came to $237 million, down from $252 million in the same quarter a year ago. Included in the quarter were $51 million in restructuring expenses, which followed the company’s disclosure in late September that it would cut about 2.5% of its workforce, mostly in its product and technology team.

Total subscription revenue backlog grew 6.1%, to $27.548 billion, with the 12-month figure up 12.3%, to $9.216 billion. Free cash flow came to $691 million, up from $550 million. During the quarter, Workday spent $750 million buying back about 3.8 million shares.

The quarter also saw Workday hold its annual Rising customer conference in Las Vegas in October, when the tech giant made Sana the newly introduced home experience for its platform. Built on technology from Sana Labs AB, which Workday acquired for about $1.1 billion last year, Sana is an AI interface that brings tasks, decisions, meetings and agent activity together in one place. Autopilot Agents, also launched at the event, are designed to handle routine HR, finance and IT processes in the background.

According to recent reports, on the opening day of Rising, Workday announced that it had agreed to acquire agentic identity platform ConductorOne Inc., better known as C1.ai. That deal closed on Monday. A partnership with Anthropic PBC, also unveiled at Rising, is set to bring Claude together with Sana AI agents and Workday’s HR and finance data.

Industry observers note that “The past few quarters have been our strongest on the innovation and invention front, and in Q3, our AI products drove nearly $150 million in upcoming ACV, more than three times what we delivered a year ago,” remarked co-founder and Chief Executive Aneel Bhusri, who returned to the top job in February after Carl Eschenbach stepped down. The priority now, Bhusri added, is to get more customers running agents in production.

According to Workday, the number of core customers that have bought at least one of its AI products rose nearly 25% from the previous quarter, to more than 2,200.

Pointing to what he called “ongoing adoption across our AI portfolio,” Chief Financial Officer Zane Rowe said the manufacturer is raising its full-year targets.

According to recent reports, for its fiscal fourth quarter, Workday expects subscription revenue of $2.6 billion, up 10%, and an adjusted operating margin of 31.7%. Full-year subscription revenue is now forecast at $9.958 billion, up 13%, compared with the $9.94 billion to $9.95 billion guided in August. The full-year adjusted operating margin forecast was also raised, to 31.5%, ahead of the 31.1% expected by analysts.

Sources indicate that though the full-year numbers moved higher, the fourth-quarter subscription forecast came in narrowly below the $2.61 billion analysts had been expecting. Growth of 10% in the period would also be a step down from the 12.8% Workday posted in the third quarter.

This score is crucial to how your ads perform and how much they cost. But what does it mean for realtors, and what constitutes a great Google Quality Real Estate Score? Let's dive in.

Google Ads Quality Score is essentially a measurement of the quality and relevance of both your keywords and PPC ads. It is a dynamic metric, assigned on a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the best possible score. It is used by Google to determine your cost per click (CPC) and your ad rank in the ad auction process.

Quality Score is calculated based on three primary components: click-through rate (CTR), ad relevance, and landing page experience.

Recent findings suggest that for any industry, including real estate, a good Quality Score is generally around 7 or above. However, in the competitive world of real estate, striving for an even higher Quality Score could give you an advantage. So, for realtors, a great Quality Score might be considered 8 or above.

According to recent reports, that noted, keep in mind that a high-Quality Score is not an end in itself. It's a sign that your ads are relevant, and your landing pages provide a good user experience, but it's still just one factor in the overall success of your Google Ads campaigns.

A high-Quality Score is beneficial for several reasons:.

Industry observers note that improving your Quality Score is all about relevance and user experience. Here are some strategies:.

It not only helps you rank higher and pay less for clicks but also ensures your ads are shown to the most relevant audiences. However, remember that Quality Score is just one piece of the puzzle. You should also consider other factors like your bidding strategy and overall account performance to create a successful Google Ads campaign.

With continuous effort and strategic planning, you can optimize your Quality Score and ultimately generate more leads for your real estate business.
